parse.title: The Sight & Sound Greatest Films of All Time 2012

wikitext.*:
==Critics' poll==
They published the critics' list of "[[List of films considered the best|greatest films]]" based on 846 critics, programmers, academics, and distributors,<ref name="bfi">{{cite web |title=The 100 Greatest Films of All Time |url=https://www.bfi.org.uk/sight-and-sound/greatest-films-all-time |website=Sight & Sound |publisher=BFI |access-date=23 March 2020}}</ref> as well as a directors' list based on 358 directors and filmmakers.<ref name="director2012">{{cite web |url=https://www.bfi.org.uk/sight-and-sound/polls/greatest-films-all-time/directors-100-best |title=Directors' 10 Greatest Films of All Time |work=Sight & Sound |publisher=British Film Institute |date=December 4, 2014}}</ref> The two lists were headed by 1958's ''[[Vertigo (film)|Vertigo]]'' and 1953's ''[[Tokyo Story]]'' respectively.

[[File:Vertigo 1958 trailer Kim Novak at Golden Gate Bridge Fort Point.jpg|thumb|[[Vertigo (film)|''Vertigo'']] (1958)]]
In the 2012 critics' poll, ''[[Vertigo (film)|Vertigo]]'' ranked first,<ref name="bfi"/><ref>{{cite web |last1=Matthews |first1=Peter |title=Vertigo rises: the greatest film of all time? |url=https://www.bfi.org.uk/sight-and-sound/polls/greatest-films-all-time/vertigo-hitchcock-new-number-one |website=Sight & Sound |publisher=BFI |access-date=23 March 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine |title=Sight & Sound's Top Fifty Films |date=2012-08-01 |magazine=[[The New Yorker]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230715072632/https://www.newyorker.com/culture/richard-brody/sight-s-top-fifty-films |archive-date=2023-07-15 |url-status=live |url=https://www.newyorker.com/culture/richard-brody/sight-s-top-fifty-films}}</ref> replacing ''[[Citizen Kane]]'', which held the top spot in the previous five [[decennial]] critics' polls.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.bfi.org.uk/films-tv-people/sightandsoundpoll2012/critics |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160207035347/http://www.bfi.org.uk/films-tv-people/sightandsoundpoll2012/critics |url-status=dead |archive-date=February 7, 2016 |title=Critics' Top 100 |year=2012 |work=Sight & Sound |publisher=British Film Institute}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Critics Top Ten Poll 2002 |work=Sight & Sound |publisher=British Film Institute |url=http://www.bfi.org.uk/sightandsound/topten/poll/critics.html |access-date=May 10, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20020816030430/http://www.bfi.org.uk/sightandsound/topten/poll/critics.html |archive-date=August 16, 2002 |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Brown |first=Mark |title=Vertigo tops greatest film poll, ending reign of Citizen Kane |url=https://www.theguardian.com/film/2012/aug/01/vertigo-hitchcock-bfi-greatest-film |newspaper=[[The Guardian]] |date=August 1, 2012 |access-date=November 26, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Vertigo is named 'greatest film of all time' |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/entertainment-arts-19078948 |publisher=[[BBC News]] |date=August 2, 2012 |access-date=November 26, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Gleiberman |first=Owen |author-link=Owen Gleiberman |title='Vertigo' over 'Citizen Kane'? Why the new Sight and Sound critics' poll is full of itself |url=https://ew.com/article/2012/08/07/the-sight-and-sound-poll-is-full-of-it/ |magazine=[[Entertainment Weekly]] |date=August 7, 2012 |access-date=November 26, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Robey |first=Tim |title=Is Alfred Hitchcock's thriller Vertigo really the best film ever made? |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/films/2016/04/19/is-alfred-hitchcocks-thriller-vertigo-really-the-best-film-ever/ |newspaper=[[The Daily Telegraph]] |date=April 29, 2016 |access-date=November 26, 2018}}</ref>

[[Dziga Vertov]]'s 1929 silent documentary ''[[Man with a Movie Camera]]'' was the only film in the top 10 that had not appeared in the critics' top 10 lists published previously.

2,045 different films received at least one mention from one of the 846 critics.
